Thanks for getting this going. I agree we may need an increase in the timeout. I'm not sure on a guess here 🤔 how long does this take for you to run the tests locally? have you run any of them recently? Just taking a look at the logs, do we have an idea of how far along clients were when it timed out? Yes but not all 😅. Plus some devnet2 branches are just not even working yet. I ran against Nimbus recently which was passing everything I was testing. Mostly specific cases that were rercently added and I wanted to double check I noticed, for example, that geth is currently syncing on consume-engine and so every single test took 30s and timed out. okay I will incrase it to 20h since we have a 24 h cadence much more does not make sense I believe this could be related I see so timing out is a sign of a client not working? shouldn't the client fail the tests rather than timing out? It seems it was looking for payloads and never receiving I will check again today A single test was taking 30s and failing at the timeout if its just timing out at a test level then we shouldn't need to increase the timeout? right Let me take a look against these logs today <@577788234810130432> it looks like Besu was passing some tests and it was a bit less than halfway through the tests at ~17,680 tests when it ran out of time... I think it is indeed a timeout issue but we may need over 24h for these runs? With the 24h cadence that's still a _trigger_ cadence right? So it shouldn't matter? so like 32h I think we can do something like that and then tune it down once we get some times out of these runs? It's a lot of tests 😅 We should probably run the EIPs/BAL specific tests in it own run (faster) then the static tests in a separate run if we are hitting over 12hrs. We do have a method to significantly increase the speed of consume engine but it requires us porting all the static tests to python!
